subject: Activation validation: stability scan & observability sampling
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Luis Ortega <luis.ortega@acme-corp.com>, ops-eng@acme-corp.com
Cc: irene_choi@redwood.ai, jordan_blake@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-09-25T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Activation validation: stability scan & observability sampling

Hi Luis / Acme ops team —

Quick note as we move into the activation window at 09:30 PT: Redwood will run a 90-minute stability scan followed by an observability sampling sweep. Scope: health-check pass rate, tail latency under load (P95/P99), KV cache priming behavior for existing traffic prefixes, and telemetry sampling to validate traces/tags reach your SIEM.

Please confirm that the firewall allowlist we shared (ports 443, 9090 for telemetry; 2222 for emergency ssh) is accepted. I’ve attached the CSV of IP ranges for reference. If you prefer, we can do a short port-check at 09:20.

Plan highlights (we'll follow the runbook linked below):
- 09:30: Canary traffic (5% of prod) -> check P95 < 150ms
- 10:00: KV cache priming: replay of top-1k prefixes, verify cache hit growth
- 10:30: Observability sampling: trace sampling at 10% with tags: account=acme, region=us-west
- 11:00: Stabilization readout and handback

Runbook: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcD-Runbook-Activation
Jira: INF-4321

Attachments: acme-fw-allowlist.csv

Thanks — I’ll be on the bridge and will post interim samples to the Jira ticket.

--
Rafael Mendes
Customer Reliability Engineer | Redwood Inference
rafael_mendes@redwood.ai

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>, Luis Ortega <luis.ortega@acme-corp.com>
Cc: jordan_blake@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-09-25T09:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Activation validation: stability scan & observability sampling

Thanks Rafael — quick checklist from infra side before we start:  
- Can we confirm BGP / NAT translation windows are complete? (Jordan, can you confirm?)
- Health check endpoints: /healthz and /live must return 200 within 500ms for the canary group.
- Telemetry endpoint (https://telemetry.acme-corp.com/collector) must accept POSTs from Redwood IP ranges listed.

Jordan: please run the BGP neighbor check and post a short packet capture snippet if anything looks off. If Acme has staged ACLs, we should run the lightweight port probe at :20 as Rafael suggested.

I’ll publish an ops-evidence sample at 10:05 with P95 snapshots and initial cache hit metrics.

--
Irene Choi
Platform PM, Private Deployments | Redwood Inference
irene_choi@redwood.ai

From: Luis Ortega <luis.ortega@acme-corp.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>, irene_choi@redwood.ai
Cc: ops-eng@acme-corp.com
Date: 2027-09-25T10:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Activation validation: stability scan & observability sampling

Rafael / Irene —

Confirmed on our side: firewall rules were pushed at 09:05 PT; allowlist attached (acme-fw-allowlist.csv). BGP neighbors are stable, and NAT translations are within expected range. We’ll accept the port-probe at 09:20.

One ask: during the KV priming step, could you exclude any query strings containing PII so we don't inadvertently cache sensitive payloads? We have a traffic-scrub policy; Jordan and I discussed a regex filter earlier. Please apply the regex: (?i) (ssn|ssn\:|social)  to the priming job.

Also, our on-call (Helena) will be on the bridge from 09:15 — adding her to the ops-eng alias.

Thanks,
Luis Ortega
Senior SRE, Acme Corp

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Luis Ortega <luis.ortega@acme-corp.com>, irene_choi@redwood.ai
Cc: jordan_blake@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-09-25T11:07:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Activation validation: stability scan & observability sampling

Thanks — good catches. We will:  
- Run the port probe at 09:20 (logged to INF-4321).
- Apply the PII exclusion regex to the priming replay job (excluded paths will be omitted from cache writes).

Interim canary observations (first 30m):
- Canary P95: 132ms; P99: 548ms (under high tail, correlating with a single node GC spike; ops team flagged and node was cycled).
- KV cache hit rate: started at 2% -> warmed to 27% after priming of top-1k prefixes.
- Telemetry: 9/10 traces reached the collector; one trace failed with TLS handshake error (we retried and it succeeded).

I’ve attached the short smoke PDF with the curated logs we promised. We’ll hold at 5% traffic for another 30 minutes and then move to 25% if no regressions.

Attachments: smoke-report-1.pdf

--
Rafael Mendes
Customer Reliability Engineer | Redwood Inference
rafael_mendes@redwood.ai

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>, irene_choi@redwood.ai, jordan_blake@redwood.ai
Cc: Luis Ortega <luis.ortega@acme-corp.com>, ops-eng@acme-corp.com
Date: 2027-09-25T16:38:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Activation validation: stability scan & observability sampling — stabilization readout

Folks — final readout and closure notes from today’s activation window:  

Summary:
- Escalation: single GC-related tail latency observed at ~09:45; node cycled and no further P99 spikes.
- KV cache: steady-state hit rate at 44% for primed prefixes after increasing traffic to 25%.
- Telemetry: sampling tags accounted for 11% of traces; all required tags (account, region, request_id) are present in the forwarded traces.
- Firewall: acme-fw-allowlist.csv verified; no blocked telemetry endpoints remaining.

Post-deploy evidence published to the runbook folder and Jira (INF-4321). See ops-evidence-sample.txt for raw metric snapshots.

Next steps / action items:
- Jordan: schedule a 1-hour follow-up to validate longer-tail KV growth patterns next week (propose Wed 09/29).
- Rafael: handover the priming config bundle and exclusion regex used into the private-runbook (link below).
- Acme: confirm if you want TTL adjustments (current default 12h) for primed keys or keep default.

Links: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcD-Runbook-Activation | Jira INF-4321
Attachments: ops-evidence-sample.txt

Thanks everyone for the quick coordination — closing this window as successful.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Sr. Ops Manager, Private Deployments | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
